objects.name: Analytic 2121
objects.description: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux service process (historian daemon, Open Platform Communications (OPC) gateway) being killed or crashing following a sustained high-rate inbound connection pattern recorded by network monitoring, correlated with daemon log entries indicating connection limit exhaustion or out-of-memory conditions. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when a device-specific traffic/resource threshold is exceeded and the same window shows service degradation, failed polling, device alarm/restart, resource exhaustion, or malformed/out-of-spec protocol behavior. Suppress planned load tests, maintenance, network convergence/failover, and known equipment faults after operator confirmation.

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: auditd:SYSCALL
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Linux Audit SYSCALL/EXECVE/SOCKADDR records (configured audit rule): Industrial Control Systems (ICS) service process terminated (SIGKILL/SIGSEGV) following high-rate inbound connections recorded in netflow within the same window

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: syslog:daemon
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) daemon log entry indicating connection limit exceeded, out of memory, or watchdog timeout

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: Network device CPU utilization percentage above which sustained load suggests packet-processing strain from flood traffic.
Connections-per-minute threshold exceeding normal SCADA polling cadence, derived from the device's actual configured scan rate.
Time window over which flood rate and subsequent device silence are correlated, typically 1-5 minutes.
Device-specific supervisory poll interval used to determine what counts as a process historian gap.
Deviation from baseline interface error/discard rate, tuned against historical interface health data.
Number of malformed/out-of-spec PDUs within the detection window constituting a flood, set above the device's documented error-tolerance baseline.
